result.summary:
REQ-194 PASSES the REVIEWER gate. Read the design (lib/letflow/design/req194-prometheus-metrics.md), SECURITY-REVIEWER's full report (security-review-req194.md), and the real diff directly (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex lib/letflow/metrics/exposition.ex lib/letflow/plugs/http_metrics.ex lib/letflow/routers/metrics_exposition.ex lib/letflow/application.ex lib/letflow/router.ex lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex lib/letflow/engine.ex lib/letflow/event_store.ex lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex mix.exs).

DEPENDENCY SIGN-OFF (REQUIRED, AC3) -- GRANTED. `{:telemetry, "~> 1.4"}` in mix.exs is a promotion of an already-resolved transitive dependency, not a new fetch: confirmed myself via `git diff main...HEAD -- mix.lock` (empty) and the mix.exs diff (+12/-0, entirely a comment plus the one line). Weighed the real alternative the design considered and rejected -- adopting telemetry_metrics/telemetry_metrics_prometheus_core -- and agree with design §10's reasoning: this subsystem has exactly six fixed, hand-specified families with a tenant-safety-critical label allow-list per family; a generic declarative reporter would still require the same hand-written label-extraction code to enforce 'never extract an identifying label,' so it buys no real reduction in reviewable surface while adding an external release cadence and, for the Prometheus-core variant, its own HTTP-exposition path to reconcile with Letflow.Router's route table. Hand-rolling was the right call. Promoting :telemetry itself to direct status (rather than continuing to borrow it opportunistically off bandit/ecto/plug's transitive graph) is correct Elixir hygiene once first-party code calls its API directly (`:telemetry.execute/3`, `:telemetry.attach_many/4`, `:telemetry.span/3` all now appear in lib/letflow/ source) -- a future Bandit/Ecto major version could otherwise drop or relocate that transitive pull with no direct pin to catch it. Zero new bytes, zero new license surface, zero new NIF/Port surface. Sign-off recorded.

SUPERVISION -- idiomatic, no startup-order hazard. Letflow.Metrics.Registry sits as a leaf child directly after {Registry, keys: :unique, name: Letflow.Registry} in application.ex; nothing looks it up during its own init/1, matching the Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry ordering precedent already in that file. The ETS table (:letflow_metrics, :set, :named_table, :public, {:write_concurrency, true}) is created and owned by the GenServer itself in init/1, not by any caller -- this is the correct ownership direction: callers (HTTP request processes, Letflow.Engine, Letflow.EventStore, Letflow.Scheduler.Poller) write directly via :ets.update_counter/:ets.insert from their OWN processes, so a caller crashing mid-write cannot corrupt or destroy the table (only the owning GenServer's own death does that, which is the intended, documented restart semantic -- counters/histograms reset on a Registry restart, an accepted Prometheus convention since rate()/increase() tolerate resets). terminate/2 calls :telemetry.detach/1, so a normal supervised restart re-attaches cleanly via init/1 with no leaked handler; even in the edge case where terminate/2 does not run before a re-attach (a :kill signal), attach_many/4's handler is a bare module-function reference (&__MODULE__.dispatch/4), not tied to the dead process instance, so a stale/duplicate attach attempt is harmless either way (attach_many failing with :already_exists on double-attach is silently ignored by init/1, but that's fine here because dispatch/4 is stateless and produces the same behavior regardless of which attach call 'won'). This is a correct, idiomatic use of the ETS-owner-GenServer pattern, not a crutch.

FOUR FLAGGED ITEMS -- idiom/design-consistency angle:
1. Dependency sign-off: see above, GRANTED.
2. Label-allowlist invariant (registry.ex): independently re-read every handle_*/dispatch clause myself. Matches SECURITY-REVIEWER's line-by-line account exactly -- each handler destructures only its own named allow-list key(s) out of metadata, never a dynamic Map.take/pass-through. From the idiom angle this is exactly the right mechanism: the safety property is enforced by function-head pattern matching (handle_task_completed/3's `when status in [...]` guard, Map.fetch!/2's explicit named keys in handle_http_request/3), which makes it a structural, grep-able property rather than a runtime promise -- no crutch here.
3. conn.private[:plug_route] correction: spot-checked deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex:663-664/520/324-327 myself: matches ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's account. http_metrics.ex's resolve_route_template/1 correctly collapses both the (unreachable-here) genuinely-absent case and the '/*_path' wildcard case to the single 'unmatched' constant with no concatenation. Idiomatic, no leak.
4. Poller DB-unavailable deviation from design §6's literal wording: agree with SECURITY-REVIEWER that this is safe. My own independent idiom/design-quality view, specifically on the failure-loop question: schedule_next_tick/0 runs UNCONDITIONALLY after the case in handle_info/2, and it always computes the SAME delay (Scheduler.poll_interval_ms() + jitter) regardless of which branch (:ok or :error) fired -- there is no faster retry path, no backoff-free tight loop, no busy-wait. Under a sustained DB outage the Poller simply keeps ticking at its normal configured cadence and calling mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0 (a true no-op) each time, which is the correct resilience pattern here: a stale gauge is the intended degradation, not a symptom to retry harder against. This is not a raise-swallowing anti-pattern (fetch_tenant_schemas/0 rescues once and returns a tagged :error result the case explicitly handles) and not a crutch. On the documentation-clarity question (separate from safety): design §6's literal 'proceeds normally' sentence is now factually wrong for the tenant_schemas/0-raises branch, and while poller.ex's own moduledoc already states the deviation prominently ('a deliberate, flagged deviation from the design's literal wording'), the design doc itself (req194-prometheus-metrics.md §6) has not been amended to match. Recommend a small follow-up (not blocking this gate): amend design §6's literal sentence to read 'the timer poll-and-fire loop for that tick is skipped along with the refresh, since both share the same failed input' so a future reader of the design doc alone (without also reading poller.ex's moduledoc) isn't misled by wording SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER both had to independently correct.

SCOPE CREEP -- none found. Diff is exactly the six OBS-02 families plus the two required emission call sites (Letflow.Engine.complete_task/3, Letflow.EventStore.append/2) plus the attachment-only family 4 (Ecto's own already-emitted event, no new call site, as designed). Confirmed no REQ-195 (audit table), REQ-201 (alerting), or web/ changes anywhere in `git diff main...HEAD --stat` (28 files, all lib/letflow/{metrics,plugs,routers,scheduler}, engine.ex, event_store.ex, application.ex, router.ex, api_pipeline.ex, mix.exs, matching test files, and handoff/status bookkeeping -- zero web/ files, zero new audit/alerting code). REQ-200 (timeline) is untouched by this diff.

DELETION OF lib/letflow/routers/metrics.ex -- complete and clean. router.ex/api_pipeline.ex forward lines removed, authorization_enforcement_test.exs and req078_supporting_routes_test.exs updated consistently (no orphaned @metrics_opts, no stale route-table entries), :MetricsRead permission atom left in place unused per design §9/§10's own explicit, non-silent open-question disposition -- correct, not an oversight. ONE MINOR, NON-BLOCKING FINDING: two pre-existing code comments were left stale by this removal and were not part of this diff's own churn -- lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1253 ('Backs GET /api/v1/metrics (Letflow.Routers.Metrics)') and lib/letflow/engine.ex:3434-3438 ('These back GET /api/v1/metrics... See Letflow.Routers.Metrics's moduledoc') both reference a module and route that no longer exist. The functions themselves (Definitions.count_definitions_by_status/1, Engine.count_instances_by_status/1, Engine.count_tasks_by_status/1) are NOT dead code -- count_instances_by_status/1 is actively reused by this very requirement's Poller refresh (poller.ex's count_active_for_schema/1) -- so this is a documentation-staleness nit only, not a functional or scope defect. Not blocking; worth a one-line comment fix in a future small pass (or folded into REQ-194's own follow-up if one is opened for the :MetricsRead cleanup).

OBSERVATION (not blocking, worth watching): Letflow.Engine.emit_task_completed_telemetry/2 (engine.ex) issues a genuine new Definitions.get_by_id/2 DB read on the request's own critical path, inside run_complete_task/6, after the completion transaction commits but before interpret_complete_result/1 returns to the caller. Design §3 states family 2's emission 'can only add microseconds of same-process ETS-counter-increment overhead (no network call, no GenServer round-trip)' -- the shipped implementation does not quite meet that framing, since resolving definition_status this way is a real DB round-trip, not just an ETS increment. This is within the discretion design §12 open question 3 explicitly granted ELIXIR-DEV ('the precise existing binding to reuse was not traced line-by-line in this design pass'), and is disclosed plainly in the function's own comment, not hidden -- so not a defect or a design violation, but if task-completion volume becomes hot enough for this extra query to matter, a future pass should look at whether definition_status is already resolvable from data run_complete_task/6 has loaded earlier in the same call (e.g. from the instance/definition it already fetched) rather than issuing a second query per completion.

Decision-record consistency: no docs/migration/decisions/ update needed and none is warranted. Checked the precedent this handoff pointed at -- 0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md is the actual 'new direct dependency' decision-record precedent (not a separate REQ-148 file), and it exists because tv-labs/lua and wasmex were genuinely NEW fetches with real surface area to vet (license, NIF/Port boundary, download counts, vendored build). {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"} has none of that -- zero new bytes, zero new license surface, zero new native/NIF/Port code, already running in-process today. A REVIEWER sign-off recorded in this PR/handoff (as done here and by SECURITY-REVIEWER) is the proportionate mechanism for a zero-risk promotion; writing a full decision record for it would be process weight the design's own §10 reasoning (and this project's own 0014 precedent) does not call for. Design doc §10's dependency framing is internally consistent with 0014 and does not silently diverge from any existing decision.

Could not independently run `mix compile`/`mix test` in this environment (no Elixir/Mix toolchain on PATH here) -- relying on ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's reported real runs (53 new tests passing, mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean, mix format --check-formatted clean, targeted + broader sweep totaling hundreds of passing tests) rather than re-deriving that result myself. Stating this limitation explicitly rather than claiming independent verification I did not perform.
